passage:
"No! No! I hate it!" Lalremsiami threw the blocks across the room and kicked the wall. Her face was red and her fists were shut.
Deepika, her mother, did not shout back. She sat on the floor a few steps away. "I'm here. I'll stay."
"Go away!" Lalremsiami screamed, then kicked again, then dropped on her tummy and wailed.
Deepika waited, saying nothing more. After a few minutes the crying slowed. Deepika opened her arms and Lalremsiami crawled in.
Later, over milk, Deepika said, "You were so angry when the tower fell. That's a big feeling. What can we do next time?"
"Kick the cushion," Lalremsiami said.

qa.q: What did Lalremsiami do to the blocks when angry?
qa.a: Lalremsiami threw the blocks across the room.

qa.q: What was Deepika feeling while Lalremsiami screamed "Go away!"?
qa.a: Deepika was probably worried but stayed calm and patient. Sitting nearby and not shouting back show a wish to keep the child feeling safe.

qa.q: What did Deepika do later over milk that taught something?
qa.a: Deepika named the feeling, "You were so angry when the tower fell," and asked what they could do next time. Lalremsiami suggested kicking the cushion.

qa.q: What might it have been like for Lalremsiami when Deepika stayed nearby?
qa.a: Lalremsiami probably felt safe enough to let the anger out and then to come back for comfort. Deepika's steady presence made the tantrum less lonely.

grounding: An angry child kicks and screams and needs help to calm, and a calm mother stays nearby and names the feeling later.

passage:
Teacher's note, Monday. Omkar, age five, was building a tall tower when another child bumped the table. Omkar screamed, kicked the leg of the table and hit the floor with both hands. I did not talk. I moved the blocks out of the way, crouched about a metre away and stayed. Omkar screamed for a few minutes, glancing to check whether I was still there.
When the screaming ran out, I said quietly, "Ready for a drink?" Omkar nodded. At the water jug I said, "You were angry that the tower fell. That was a big, cross feeling." Omkar said, "I wanted it to stay." We built a smaller tower together.
Varun, class teacher

qa.q: What did Omkar do when the table was bumped?
qa.a: Omkar screamed, kicked the leg of the table and hit the floor with both hands.

qa.q: What was Varun feeling and thinking while waiting a metre away?
qa.a: Varun stayed calm and patient, knowing talking would not help yet. Moving the blocks aside and staying close shows a wish to keep Omkar safe.

qa.q: What did Varun do that helped Omkar calm down?
qa.a: Varun stayed close without talking, moved the blocks aside and waited. Later Varun named the feeling: "You were angry that the tower fell."

qa.q: What might it have been like for Omkar when Varun stayed nearby without talking?
qa.a: Omkar was angry about the tower and also wanted to know Varun was still close, glancing to check. Having someone nearby made the anger feel less frightening.

grounding: An angry child kicks and screams, and a calm teacher stays nearby and names the feeling after the child calms.

passage:
The supermarket queue was long, the air-conditioning was broken, and Lokesh wanted the chocolate at the counter. Deepika said no. Lokesh screamed, threw himself on the floor and kicked the trolley.
People stared. Deepika's face went hot. She wanted to drag him up and shout.
Instead she crouched beside him, out of kicking reach, and waited. She didn't lecture. "I'm right here."
He screamed on, then slowed to sobs. She held out her arms, and he crawled in.
In the car she said softly, "You were really angry about the chocolate."
He nodded into her shoulder. "Very angry."

qa.q: What did Lokesh want at the counter?
qa.a: Lokesh wanted the chocolate at the counter.

qa.q: What was Deepika feeling when people stared?
qa.a: Deepika felt embarrassed and frustrated, her face going hot, tempted to drag him up and shout.

qa.q: What did Deepika do that helped Lokesh calm down?
qa.a: She stayed calm and close without lecturing, waited for the storm to pass, and named his anger later in the car.

qa.q: What was the tantrum like for Lokesh?
qa.a: Lokesh was overwhelmed by anger he couldn't control, and felt comforted when she stayed near and held him.

grounding: An angry child kicks and screams, and a calm adult stays near, waits, and names the feeling afterwards.

passage:
At the Mumbai day-care, Sumit's tower of blocks was knocked over by another boy. Sumit screamed, threw a block and kicked the wall, his face red.
Asif Sir moved the other children back and knelt a little distance away. He didn't tell Sumit to stop or ask why. He just said, low and calm, "I'm here. I'll wait."
Sumit kicked, then cried, then sat down hard, hiccupping.
Asif Sir moved closer. "You were so angry when your tower fell."
Sumit nodded. "I made it so tall."
"Want to build it again? I'll help."

qa.q: What knocked over Sumit's tower?
qa.a: Another boy knocked over Sumit's tower of blocks.

qa.q: What was Sumit feeling when he said "I made it so tall"?
qa.a: Sumit felt sad and disappointed that the tall tower he was proud of had fallen.

qa.q: Why did Asif Sir wait before talking?
qa.a: Sumit was too upset to listen, so staying calm and nearby helped him settle first, and naming the anger afterwards helped him understand it.

qa.q: How might the other children see Asif Sir's response?
qa.a: They might feel safe and reassured, seeing a calm adult handle a big outburst without shouting.

grounding: An angry child kicks and screams, and a calm adult stays nearby and names the feeling once the child is calmer.

passage:
"Aditi, it's time to switch off the cartoon."
"NO! NO! I'm watching!"
"Mama is here."
"Go away! I hate you!"
Pema sat on the floor near the door, not too close. She waited.
"I HATE bath!"
Aditi kicked the cushion and screamed into it. Pema stayed quiet.
After a while, Aditi's screams became sniffles.
"Can I come close?"
A tiny nod.
Pema held her. "You were very angry that the cartoon ended."
"Very very angry."
"I know. It's hard to stop fun things."
"Can I bring my duck in the bath?"
"Yes, the duck can come."

qa.q: What did Aditi kick?
qa.a: Aditi kicked the cushion.

qa.q: Why did Aditi scream "I hate you"?
qa.a: Aditi was furious and overwhelmed that her cartoon was ending, and the angry words poured out.

qa.q: What did Pema do well?
qa.a: She stayed calm and nearby without arguing, asked before coming close, and named Aditi's anger once the storm passed.

qa.q: What might Pema have been feeling during the screaming?
qa.a: Pema may have felt hurt or tired hearing "I hate you", but she stayed calm and patient.

grounding: An angry child screams and kicks, and a calm parent stays nearby and names the feeling once the child calms.

passage: Teacher's note, Tuesday, playground. When Yusuf got the swing first, Darshan screamed, kicked the sand and threw his shoe. I didn't lecture. I moved the other children back a little and sat on the low wall nearby, close but quiet. "I'm here," I said, once. Darshan kept screaming for a while, then sobbing, then just breathing hard. After about five minutes he crawled over and leaned on my knee. Only then did I say, "You were so angry. You wanted the swing." He nodded. We did a big dragon breath together, and he asked Yusuf for the next turn.

qa.q: What did Darshan throw?
qa.a: His shoe.

qa.q: What does Darshan leaning on the teacher's knee suggest?
qa.a: It suggests his anger had burnt down and he felt safe enough to look for comfort.

qa.q: What could another adult copy from the teacher when a child is screaming?
qa.a: Stay close and quiet, keep others safe, say "I'm here", and name the feeling only once the child has calmed.

qa.q: Why might the teacher have waited to name the feeling?
qa.a: The teacher seemed to know Darshan could not take in words while screaming, so calm presence came first and words came once he settled.

grounding: Shows an angry small child kicking and screaming, and a calm adult who stays nearby and names the feeling only after he calms.
